pages.title: New mod starter kit
pages.description: What a new mod needs to know: when to delete, time out or ban, handling common situations and hate raids, and good habits.
pages.content:
Welcome to the team. This page covers what most streamers expect from a new mod. Your streamer's own rules always come first, so read those too and ask when something isn't clear.

## Your job in one line

Keep chat a place people want to stay in, without making it about you. Most of modding is quiet: deleting a message, a short timeout, answering a question.

## Before your first stream

- Read the channel's rules and ask the streamer what they care about most (spoilers? backseating? self-promo?).
- Turn on **Mod View** on Twitch and get comfortable with the user card: account age, past messages and mod notes.
- Join the mod chat (usually a private Discord channel) and say hi.
- Ask which bot the channel uses (Fossabot, Nightbot...) and whether you'll have dashboard access.
- Learn the panic buttons: Shield Mode, followers-only and slow mode. See the [command cheat sheet](/commands).

## Delete, timeout or ban?

Go up the ladder only as far as you need to:

1. **Delete the message** for one-off mistakes (a spoiler, a link without permission).
2. **Short timeout** (1 to 10 minutes) for someone who keeps going after a reminder.
3. **Longer timeout** (hours) for repeated or deliberate trouble.
4. **Ban** for things that should never be in chat.

Ban straight away, no warning needed, for: hate speech and slurs, threats, sharing someone's personal information, sexual content, obvious bots and spam accounts, and ban evasion.

Always add a short reason (`/timeout username 600 spoilers`). It tells the chatter why, and tells the other mods what happened.

## Common situations

- **Spam and bot links:** delete, ban the account if it's clearly a bot, and add the phrase to the channel's blocked terms. The [blocked-terms generator](/blocked-terms) helps catch the misspellings too.
- **Backseating:** a friendly reminder first, a short timeout if it keeps happening.
- **Spoilers:** delete and remind. Follow the streamer's rule on how strict to be.
- **Self-promo:** delete links and "come watch my stream" messages unless the streamer allows them.
- **Chatters arguing:** step in early and calmly in chat; if it carries on, time out both sides briefly.
- **The streamer is being targeted:** act quietly and quickly. Don't draw attention to it on stream.

## If a hate raid starts

1. Turn on **Shield Mode** (`/shield`), or followers-only and slow mode if it isn't set up.
2. Clear the worst messages and ban the raiding accounts.
3. Don't argue with them in chat; that's what they want.
4. Tell the other mods in mod chat so you're not doubling up.
5. Afterwards, report the accounts to Twitch and turn the modes back off.

## Good habits

- Be consistent: the same thing should get the same response, whoever says it.
- Never use mod powers for personal disagreements.
- Keep mod-chat and mod-only information private.
- When you're unsure, a short timeout and a question in mod chat beats a ban you'll have to undo.
- Leave a mod note on users you've had to deal with, so the next mod has context.

## Useful tools

- [Mod command cheat sheet](/commands): Twitch, Fossabot and Nightbot commands
- [Blocked-terms generator](/blocked-terms): filter misspellings and test messages
- [Mod resources](/pages/mod-resources): official Twitch and Discord guides

pages.title: My stream setup
pages.description: The gear and small setup choices behind my streams.
pages.content:
## My current setup

I keep the current gear list on the [Tools page](/what-i-use). It includes my PC, Wooting keyboard, Stream Decks, Wave:3 microphone, and other desk equipment.

## What this guide covers

I’m building this into a practical reference for my setup: what each piece is for, what I like about it, and the resources I actually use. I’ll add details as I have useful, firsthand notes to share.

For now, the gear list is the most up-to-date reference.
